name: veterinary_clinic_system_041_noshow_fee_flag
instruction: Charge the clinic's standard no-show fee for every missed appointment. The fee is a flat $25.00. For each appointment with status 'no_show' that does not already have a no-show fee invoice for this batch: (1) set follow_up='call_owner' on the appointment; (2) create a billing invoice {invoice_number: 'NS-<batch_code>-<appointment_id>', status: 'draft', owner_id from the patient, patient_id from the appointment, location_id from the appointment, issued_date and due_date set to the episode date, total_amount: 25.00, line_items: [{description: 'No-show fee', quantity: 1, unit_price: 25.00}]}; (3) push an audit_log row {actor:'system', actor_role:'system', action:'NO_SHOW_FEE', target_collection:'billing_invoices', target_id:<new invoice id>, details:'No-show fee invoice <invoice_number> for appointment <appointment_id> (<batch_code>)', occurred_at: episode timestamp}. Finally, push one ops_reports row report='no_show_fee_summary' keyed by batch_code with {total_no_shows, total_fees, by_location: JSON object mapping location_id to fee count}. Do not alter non-no-show appointments, do not duplicate invoices on rerun, and do not touch existing billing invoices.
_steps_note: par_steps and max_steps cannot be measured in a codegen-only session. They must be recorded from a live gold run in the QC container.

success_criteria.summary: Recompute the no-show set from live appointments. Every no_show row must have follow_up='call_owner' and all other fields unchanged. There must be exactly one new billing invoice per no_show with the expected invoice_number pattern and exact fields (owner joined through patients, $25.00 total, one line item). There must be exactly one audit_log row per new invoice with exact fields. There must be exactly one ops_reports no_show_fee_summary row for this batch with total_no_shows, total_fees, and by_location counts, all derived two independent ways (Python filter and SQL) and agreeing. All other collections, including existing billing_invoices, are byte-identical.

checks.expect: one invoice+audit per no_show, summary row with exact counts
total no-shows, total fees, and per-location counts agree between Python filter and SQL

hazards: Non-no-show appointments (scheduled, confirmed, completed, checked_in) are decoys: ~482 of 548 appointments must remain untouched, including their follow_up field. A bulk 'set follow_up on everything' solution fails the byte-identity canary.
No-show fee invoices are batch-keyed by invoice_number 'NS-<batch_code>-<id>'. A solution that uses a fixed or missing batch code will create duplicates on rerun or collide with other episodes.

The owner_id must come from the patient referenced by the appointment, not from the appointment itself (which lacks owner_id). Hardcoding an owner or using appointment.location_id as owner will misroute every invoice.
The $25.00 flat fee is not in fee_schedules. A solution that picks the WELL-EXAM ($62) or SICK-EXAM ($85) price will produce the wrong invoice total and fail the exact-cents check.
No-show appointments are in the past (2026-08-05 to 2026-09-03) relative to the episode. A solution that charges only future no-shows will find none and fail.

Existing billing_invoices (260 rows, INV-1001...INV-1260) are outside the agent's target set and must remain byte-identical. A solution that appends fees to existing invoices instead of creating new ones will corrupt them and fail.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Hardmode v2 expands the v1 single-field update into a billing-and-audit workflow across four collections. It requires a patient-to-owner join, a fixed-policy fee amount, batch-keyed invoice numbering, and idempotent rerun safety. All derived numbers (totals and per-location counts) are dual-path verified.
